voyage.name: Black Sea
voyage.content: Enjoy the waves and admire the beach, the port, and the Ottoman-era clock tower

voyage.name: Music fountain
voyage.content: A nice spectacle at night where fountains are operated to the sound of and music.

voyage.name: Batumi Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Georgia has a remarkable tradition of (royal) botanical gardens. It is a quiet spot, next to the Black Sea on a high cliff and it both green and cool. Plan on a visit here to take a half day to nearly a full day as it is very large. Expensive by Georgian standards but definitely worth seeing.

voyage.name: Medea statue
voyage.content: Statue of Medea and the Golden Fleece, near the Iranian/Azerbaijani joint consulate.

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Mother of God
voyage.content: Georgian Orthodox

voyage.name: Church of the Holy Spirit
voyage.content: Roman Catholic

voyage.name: Armenian Cathedral of Christ the Savior
voyage.content: Built in 1885-87, this imposing church is fronted by a bell tower and was built diagonally to the street grid in the heart of old town Batumi.

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: Surprisingly good little museum with helpful and friendly staff. Georgian, Russian and English info and guides. Thorough background info, foreign coins, bronze vessels, glassware, ceramic, etc. Good collection of classical vases. Somewhat unpredictable opening hours.

voyage.name: Adjara Art Museum
voyage.content: Paintings of famous Georgian and foreign artists, sculptures and some samples of decorative art.

voyage.name: The Nobel Brothers Batumi Technological Museum
voyage.content: Exhibits inventions introduced to Batumi at the end of 19th - beginning of 20th centuries by Nobel Brothers, Rotschilds and Mantashev.

voyage.name: Khariton Akhvlediani Museum
voyage.content: Houses archaeological materials of XII-IX c.c. B.C

voyage.name: Makhuntseti Bridge and Waterfall
voyage.content: This is a nice half day trip with a great waterfall and an impressive strong bridge, even though she looks like collapsing every instance. In summer, people jump from the bridge into the water, so bring a towel if you dare. There is a nice 4-6-hr hike from Zeda Makhuntseti (up behind the waterfall) and then down into Kveda Makhuntseti again.

voyage.name: Remains of Gonio Fortress
voyage.content: Located at the sea shore the ruins host stunning views and interesting architecture.

voyage.name: Petra Fortress
voyage.content: Early medieval complex.

voyage.name: Panoramic Wheel
voyage.content: Attraction total time : 7min.

voyage.name: Cable car
voyage.content: Goes directly to the small (about 250 m height) nearby hill with a nice restaurant on top of it. Stunning views, especially at night.

voyage.name: Boat tour
voyage.content: Lots of boats offering boat tours. Yacht can also be chartered.

voyage.name: 6 May Park
voyage.content: Nice park with Nurigeli Lake in the middle of it. There is also a zoo corner in the northern part of it, but some animals (monkeys in particular) are kept in quite a tiny cages, so animal lovers might not enjoy it.

voyage.name: Batumi Puppet and youth state Theatre
Black Sea Jazz Festival
voyage.content: Annual Jazz festival.

voyage.name: Mt. Chakvistavi
voyage.content: Great national park for hiking with an interesting subtropical forest. The round track passes at least three climate zones, subtropical, temperate and alpine. There are some guesthouses just before the sealed road ends from Chakvi. Hiking is possible already at the beginning of April, but expect some snow at the turn at the top. There are several places along the track to get water (springs or taps) and some places t

voyage.name: Two Mountains Trail
voyage.content: Around Mt. Chakvistavi there are also other interesting hikes and trails available, like this one—even though not maintained very well.Download trail coordinates: GPX, KML.

voyage.name: Goodwill Supermarket
voyage.content: Many goods not available in smaller shops. Many of the products come from Germany.

voyage.name: Carrefour
voyage.content: Supermarket at the Black Sea Mall

voyage.name: Metro City Forum
voyage.content: Shopping mall

voyage.name: Nikora Supermarket
voyage.content: Georgian supermarket chain operating at several locations in Batumi.

voyage.name: Fish market
voyage.content: Since Batumi is also a seaport, you have to try the fish here! Head to the local Fish Market, buy some of your choice and take with you to your ho(s)tel, or let it be prepared at one of the many restaurants there. Preparation costs 3-5 lari, plus the fish 20-30 lari per kg. Salmon is quite cheap, flounder a little more expensive. Take some Ojakhuri or mashed potatoes with the fish. Btw. it is better to buy the fish y

voyage.name: Kozlovichi
voyage.content: Great atmospheric place in town. Homemade delicious food and local Batumi beer. Grandmothers cook very tasty.

voyage.name: Maspindzeli-First Adjarian Restaurant
voyage.content: Very nice place with good atmosphere and delicious Georgian cuisine. If you want to try perfect Adjarian dishes in town go here.

voyage.name: Batumis Shawarma
voyage.content: Excellent shawarma. Everything is very simple and delicious.

voyage.name: Mary's Irish Bar Batumi
voyage.content: Tasty food: great burgers and delicious Irish breakfast. Vegetarian options available. Ten beer taps. Friendly and warm atmosphere. The most comfortable pub in town.

voyage.name: Adjara
voyage.content: A wide variety of different kinds of local and international food (khachapuris, pkhalis, pakhlava etc.) If you crave for something sweet then their brownie is something for you. They have free Wi-Fi and a friendly English-speaking staff.

voyage.name: Literary cafe
voyage.content: This upscale bookstore-cafe has a number of branches in Tbilisi (in Kala, Vake, Vera, and Saburtalo), but the Batumi location is all the more attractive given the relative dearth of good and service-oriented restaurants in Batumi. Coffees, cakes, and basic Georgian sandwiches (plus khachapuri and lobiani) all available, although the menu seems more like a guideline to what might be available on any given day rather t

voyage.name: Cafe Privet iz Batuma
voyage.content: This charming "colonial Russia" theme cafe is a Batumi institution, with Georgians as well as foreigners peopling its picturesque outdoor tables. The menu is short on hot dishes, but the many kinds of blinis are delicious.

voyage.name: Radio Kitchen & Bar
voyage.content: Good place to go if you are looking for non-Georgian food in Batumi. Good choice of wine and cocktails. Staff are very friendly.

voyage.name: Restaurant Sanremo
voyage.content: Elegant, with good Georgian and international food.

voyage.name: Munich
voyage.price: US$15 for one course meal per person
voyage.content: Restaurant with German traditional cuisine. Pizza, Seafood and Vegan dishes are also served. Paying: Visa, American Express, Mastercard and Cash. Restaurant has open-air seats also. A bit overpriced.

voyage.name: Sinner's Bar & Kitchen
voyage.content: Sinner's Bar has a unique menu with over 50 different shots, fire towers, drinking challenges, buckets of chicken wings and a great selection of draft & bottled beer in Batumi.

voyage.name: Batumi Hostel
voyage.content: Comfortable hostel in a nice house in the middle of the old town. Entrance is camouflaged. Discounts available in and from Friends Hostel in the old town of Tbilisi. Free Wi-Fi. Laundry. Private room also available. Two showers and bathroom, kitchen, view on piazza and sea from balcony. Seasonal property (opened for 2012 season in May).

voyage.name: Hostel in Batumi
voyage.content: Excellent place run by a Welshman, an American and a Georgian woman. This place is fun and relaxing, and in a great location. If you're adventurous sleep on the top level of the 3 storey bunkbeds.

voyage.name: Globus Hostel Batumi
voyage.phone: +995 593 59 60 96 (Call ahead or the door may be locked)
voyage.content: Rooms are bright and clean. The hostel is new and fresh. Air conditioning, free laundry, free Wi-fi, free sheets and towels, free maps, free tea and coffee 24h. Discounts in local cafés and in Rover Hostel Tbilisi.

voyage.name: Gulnasi's Guesthouse
voyage.content: It's possible to use the kitchen; hot showers, Wi-Fi, free meals will be offered frequently. Outside the summer season the same place is also a school for small children but in the summer season the kids will be on vacation. This may be the best budget option with wheelchair access.

voyage.name: Hostel Retro
voyage.content: One of the better hostels in the city, which has maintained its good rating over the years. Smallish, friendly. The owners and volunteers are welcoming and helpful. Great vibe to the place, seems to attract a real community of travellers. Excellent khachapuri from the bakery next door. Largely Russian-speaking but has friendly and fluent English-speaking volunteers, there are always at least a few English-speaking gu

voyage.name: Sky Hostel
voyage.content: A useful option if other places are full. Kitchen but no fridge. Wi-Fi and laundry are available. Most staff don't know a lot of English.

voyage.name: Hotel Black Sea Star
voyage.content: Reasonably clean. A/C, wifi, breakfast available. View from balcony on top is noteworthy.

voyage.name: Hotel Lavro
voyage.price: A room for with no bathroom costs 20 lari (summer 2005). Reasonably clean, hot water

voyage.name: Hotel Ritsa
voyage.price: 60-100 lari for two people, breakfast included
voyage.content: Clean, smart and modern hotel located in the old town.

voyage.name: Sputnik Boutique Hotel
voyage.price: 70 lari for standard rooms with queen size beds
voyage.content: Quiet environment, great view of Batumi.

voyage.name: Sheraton Batumi Hotel
voyage.content: Direct beach access and friendly service. 203 rooms including 26 suites.

voyage.name: Intourist Palace
voyage.content: Grand, spacious with all amenities.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Batumi
voyage.content: Designed by Italian architect Michele De Lucchi, located on the beachfront near business district.

voyage.name: Hilton Batumi
voyage.content: Between a park and the sea, in the middle of the city.
